PART 01 · SETUP
uv
One fast tool for Python versions, virtual environments and packages.
uv · install
Install uv once, use it everywhere
macOS / Linux
$ curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Windows
> powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
Or with
winget install --id=astral-sh.uv -e · brew install uv · pip install uv
Check it
$ uv --version # update later with: uv self update
Replaces
pip
venv
pyenv
pipx
pip-tools
poetry
· written in Rust by Astral, 10–100× faster than pip

AI IN CODE · 01 UV
uv · cheat sheet
The nine commands you’ll actually use
uv init my-app
Create a project: pyproject.toml, main.py and a git repo
uv python install 3.12
Download and manage Python versions
uv add pandas
Install a package and record it in pyproject.toml
uv add --dev pytest
A dependency for development only
uv remove pandas
Uninstall it and update the lock file
uv run main.py
Run anything inside the project’s environment
uv sync
Rebuild the exact environment from uv.lock
uvx ruff check .
Run a tool once, without installing it
uv tool install ruff
Install a command-line tool for good

git & GitHub
Agents can change dozens of files in seconds. git is how you see every change, and undo it.
git · the mental model
Four places your code lives
Working directory
The files you and the agent edit

Staging area
The changes picked for the next snapshot
git commit
Local repository
Saved snapshots, on your machine
git push
GitHub
The shared copy: backup, pull requests, teamwork
git pull · bring GitHub’s changes to your machine
git status and git diff tell you what changed, at any moment.

AI IN CODE · 03 CHATBOTS
Chatbots · context is everything
Bad context in, bad answer out
✗ VAGUE PROMPT
Make a model that predicts who survives the Titanic.
Result: generic code, guessed column names, and missing ages crash it.
✓ SPECIFIC PROMPT
I have titanic.csv with columns PassengerId, Survived, Pclass, Name, Sex, Age, SibSp, Parch, Ticket, Fare, Cabin, Embarked. Age has 177 missing values. Using pandas and scikit-learn, train a RandomForest to predict Survived from Pclass, Sex and Age. Fill missing ages with the median and print the accuracy on an 80/20 split.
Result: code that runs first time. But you typed all of that, and pasted it again in every new chat.

Autocomplete
The first time AI moved into the editor: it reads your file and suggests the next lines.
Autocomplete · ghost text
Write a comment, press Tab
Interactive web embed: not captured for export
Tab
Accept the suggestion
Esc
Dismiss it

Next suggestion

New: next edit suggestions. Copilot predicts your next change anywhere in the file. Tab to jump, Tab to accept.
AI IN CODE · 04 AUTOCOMPLETE · shortcuts for GitHub Copilot in VS Code
Demo 1 · GitHub Copilot in VS Code
Four comments, four suggestions
example.py · one comment at a time, then Tab
# 1. Print a welcome message # 2. Greet a passenger by name # 3. Read titanic.csv with pandas # 4. Show the first 10 rows
$ uv run example.py
Great at
  • Boilerplate and repetitive code
  • Following the patterns in your file
  • Docstrings, tests, small helpers
  • Keeping you in the flow
Where it stops
  • Sees mostly the file you have open
  • Can’t run code or edit other files
  • You still drive, line by line
The best known: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, since 2021. Also: Cursor Tab, Windsurf, Tabnine, JetBrains AI.

PART 05 · AI IN YOUR APPS
Into the IDE
The model moves into the IDE and onto your desktop, and becomes an agent that reads and edits your project.
AI in your apps · the IDEs
Agents move into the editor
MICROSOFT
VS Code
Copilot’s agent mode edits files and runs commands, in the most used editor.
ANYSPHERE
Cursor
A VS Code fork built around AI: smart Tab completion plus an agent.
GOOGLE
Antigravity
Agent-first IDE: a Manager view runs several agents in parallel, with plans and browser recordings.
EXTRA · LOCAL
Zed
A fast editor written in Rust that also runs local models through Ollama.
Desktop apps too. The Claude and Codex apps install on your computer, open your folders and edit your files.

AI IN CODE · 05 APPS
Demo 2 · agent in the IDE
The Titanic web app, in one prompt
PROMPT · AGENT PANEL IN ANTIGRAVITY, CURSOR OR VS CODE
This Python project is managed with uv and has titanic.csv (the Kaggle Titanic dataset). 1. Create train.py: train a RandomForestClassifier to predict Survived from Pclass, Sex (0 = male, 1 = female) and Age (fill missing ages with the median). Print the accuracy on an 80/20 split and save the model to model.joblib. Run it with uv run. 2. Create app/main.py with FastAPI: a home page and a POST /predict endpoint that takes class, sex and age as JSON and returns the survival probability (validate class 1–3 and age 0–100). 3. Create app/templates/index.html with Tailwind via CDN: clean dark design, the title “Would you survive the Titanic?”, a simple form and the result as a percentage with a bar. 4. Write a README.md with the exact uv commands to train the model and start the app. Install anything missing with uv add and confirm the app starts.
Then
Read the plan
Review the diff
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload

AI IN CODE · 06 CLI · code.claude.com/docs
Claude Code · how to work with it
Explore, plan, code, commit
01
Explore
Let it read before it writes.
Read app/ and train.py. Don’t write code yet.
02
Plan
Shift + Tab into plan mode.
Plan a /stats endpoint. Ask me if unsure.
03
Code
Approve, then let it work.
Implement the plan. Run uv run pytest.
04
Commit
Small steps you can review.
Commit with a clear message and open a PR.
The most common mistake: jumping straight to “build it”. Ten minutes of exploring and planning saves an hour of undoing.

AI IN CODE · 06 CLI
Claude Code · costs and limits
Tokens are the currency
Everything counts
Files read, the conversation and every tool output use tokens.
Bigger model, bigger bill
Opus costs more than Sonnet, and Sonnet more than Haiku.
Know your numbers
/usage shows your plan limits; /cost shows API spend.
Spend less
/clear between tasks, /compact long chats, a good CLAUDE.md, precise prompts.
Two ways to pay: a Claude subscription comes with usage limits; an API key pays per token.

Claude Code · superpowers
MCP, subagents and skills
MCP
A standard plug for tools and data: browsers, databases, GitHub, Figma…
claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
Subagents
Specialists with their own context window. They work in parallel and report back.

Skills

.claude/skills/ uv-python/SKILL.md
AI IN CODE · 06 CLI
Claude Code · skills
A skill in ten lines
What it is
A folder with a SKILL.md: instructions, plus optional scripts and files.
How it loads
Only the description stays in context. Claude loads the rest when it’s relevant, or when you type /uv-python.
Where it lives
.claude/skills/ for the project, shared in git. ~/.claude/skills/ just for you.
.claude/skills/uv-python/SKILL.md
--- name: uv-python description: Use whenever installing packages or running Python scripts or tests. --- # Python with uv - Never use pip or python directly. - Add dependencies: uv add <package> - Run scripts: uv run <file> - Run tests: uv run pytest

Claude Code · plugins and hooks
Install a plugin, automate with a hook
Plugins
One install bundles skills, subagents, hooks and MCP servers. The official marketplace is built in.
/plugin install commit-commands@claude-plugins-official
→ adds commands to commit, push and open pull requests
# a community marketplace /plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman /plugin install caveman@caveman
Hooks
Your script runs on every matching event, every time. No reminders needed.
{ "hooks": { "PostToolUse": [{   "matcher": "Edit|Write",   "hooks": [{ "type": "command",     "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path' | xargs uvx ruff format" }] }]}}
→ in .claude/settings.json: every file Claude edits gets formatted

Claude Code · autonomy
More autonomy needs a safety net
LAYER 1
Checkpoints
Every edit is saved. Go back to the code, the conversation or both.
Esc Esc · /rewind
LAYER 2
git
Checkpoints miss changes made by shell commands. git catches everything.
git commit before big tasks
LAYER 3
Permission rules
Allow what is safe, deny what is not.
allow: Bash(uv run pytest:*) deny: Read(./.env)
Going autonomous: accept edits, or auto mode (--permission-mode auto), where Claude approves routine actions itself. These layers make that safe.

A chatbot that does the maths with tools

“How many women were on board?”

Picks a tool and writes its arguments
query_data("(df.Sex == 'female').sum()")

Runs pandas on titanic.csv, read-only
314
4 · ANSWER
314 WOMEN WERE ON BOARD STOP
The model never counts. It decides what to run; Python does the maths. Claude Code works the same way: its tools are Read, Edit and Bash.

AI IN CODE · WRAP-UP
Wrap-up · good habits
Five rules for coding with AI
01
Review everything
The code you accept is yours, bugs included.
02
Give context
Goal, files, constraints. CLAUDE.md does it every time.
03
Test
Tests catch what review misses. Let the agent run them.
04
Protect secrets
No keys, passwords or customer data in prompts.
05
Commit often
git is your undo button. Use it before every big prompt.
